answer: A sybil tax stops fake identities. Each agent pays a sunk 50-credit tax at dawn of its first epoch and ties its opal badge, a non-transferable credential, to one thread of past work. Validators check badge and thread before granting a slot. Minting 1,000 fakes costs 1,000 x 50 = 50,000 credits, and replacements pay again, while rewards split across fakes. An honest agent pays once and keeps undiluted rewards, so faking costs more than it earns.
